verdict: The accepted Nature Communications version keeps the title, abstract, data and model, and changes the main text by argument rather than new measurement. The additions answer likely requests to exclude surface electric-dipole and demagnetization mechanisms, to place the nonlinear Edelstein effect next to the inverse Faraday and Cotton-Mouton effects with new references, and to support the two-component 45-degree picture with a new superposition panel (Fig. 3d). Error bars are now defined, data moved to a Source Data file, and time-resolved XMCD is named as future validation. The Supplementary text of the new version was not available, so changes there cannot be judged. Most of the old review's measurement requests (field dependence, heating, absorbed fluence, second crystal, dynamical model) were not taken up in the main text.

inferred_requests.title: Rule out surface and conventional (non-magnetic) THz emission mechanisms
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely questioned whether the fourfold pattern and the 45-degree behaviour could come from surface electric-dipole emission (as in CrSiTe3), photo-Dember or ultrafast demagnetization rather than magnetic-dipole emission from a light-induced magnetization. The authors added arguments and references, and a caveat about the detected projection, but no new control measurement in the main text.

inferred_requests.title: Place the nonlinear Edelstein effect among known optical spin-generation mechanisms
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely asked how the effect differs from the inverse Faraday and inverse Cotton-Mouton effects and from related theory of nonlinear or dynamic spin generation, and asked for citations. The introduction gained a comparison, a microscopic note on Te bands and new theory references.

inferred_requests.title: Support the two-component (M_y and M_z) interpretation of the 45-degree data
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for evidence that the polarity reversal and minimum come from interference of two magnetization components. The authors added a superposition test (new Fig. 3d panel) and the far-field projection formula.

inferred_requests.title: Show that the magnetization itself is manipulated
inferred_requests.text: A referee likely noted that THz emission alone does not show a change of the ferromagnetic moment and asked for a direct magnetic probe or a narrower claim. The authors added only a future-work sentence naming time-resolved XMCD and softened framing in the introduction; title and abstract are unchanged.

inferred_requests.title: Define the error bars and the plotted quantity
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked how the error bars in Figs. 2f, 4c and 4e were obtained. Both captions now define them from the spread over Fourier-transform windows.

inferred_requests.title: State what the detection geometry measures
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked whether the full THz field vector was measured. The text now states that only the p-projection is detected.

inferred_requests.title: Clarify what magnetization the model describes (spot average, domains)
inferred_requests.text: A referee may have asked how a single-domain Landau model applies to a macroscopic illuminated spot. The text now says the model treats the net magnetization averaged over the beam spot.

inferred_requests.title: Make the data available
inferred_requests.text: Data availability changed from on request to a Source Data file. This is probably journal policy, possibly also a referee request.

inferred_requests.title: Temper the framing of the mechanism
inferred_requests.text: The introduction now says the authors 'attribute' the effect and 'argue' the magnetic density 'may act' as an internal field. This could answer a request to present the mechanism as an interpretation. The abstract still says 'demonstrate' and 'quantitatively captured'.

inferred_requests.title: State the conditions for generality of the mechanism
inferred_requests.text: The outlook now gives a symmetry condition for extending the mechanism to other ordered phases. A referee may have asked how general the claim of wide applicability is.

issue_status.reason: A surface-emission paragraph, a demagnetization argument and a p-projection caveat were added, but none of the requested discriminating measurements (field, transmission, thickness, both components, reference sample).
Time-resolved XMCD is named as future validation and the introduction is softened, but no direct magnetic probe was added and the title and abstract are unchanged.
Error bars in Fig. 2f are now defined; the text still claims a rapid reduction upon crossing Tc and no model curve or finer maps were added.
Only a sentence on averaging over the beam spot was added; zero-field domains, field history and the use of static M_z are not discussed.
The static Landau and mean-field treatment is unchanged in the main text.
No heating estimate appears in the main text and 'non-thermal' stays in the abstract and discussion; the Supplementary text was not available to check.
'several V/cm' is unchanged and no magnitude estimate was added to the main text.
No absorbed-fluence or reference-quantity data; the saturation is still read as magnetic.
A superposition test (Fig. 3d) and a demagnetization argument were added; no signed maps at several fluences or two-source fits.
'quantitatively captured' is kept in the abstract; parameters and the fluence mapping are not given in the main text.
The far-field projection n_z M_y - n_y M_z is now written out; Fresnel factors and refraction are not discussed in the main text.
Polar plots and the crystal-axis test are unchanged in the main text.
The introduction now contrasts the effect with inverse Faraday and Cotton-Mouton effects and names Te-dominated bands; no material-specific estimate in the main text.
No comparison of pattern shape with saturation was added.
Error bars are now defined; sample count, surface preparation and a second crystal are not reported in the main text.
No polarization-purity check is mentioned.
No photon-energy dependence was added.
The fluence calibration is in the Supplementary Information, which was not available for the new version; nothing changed in the main text.
The THz field calibration is in the Supplementary Information, not available for the new version.
Captions now tie the plotted amplitude to an extracted spectral weight; Tc is still given as about 66 K in the text.
Supplementary magnetization data could not be checked; no main-text change.
'comparable amplitudes but opposite polarity' is unchanged.
The Fig. 4 caption gained error-bar definitions and a colour key, but its garbled first sentence and the axis labels are unchanged.
The text still cites 'Fig. 4a, b' for normal incidence and 'Fig. 4c, d' for 45 degrees.
The tensor notation is unified and 'out-of-place' corrected; 'sub-valent' and the S_THz/E_THz mix remain.
Data are now provided in a Source Data file.

unaddressed_major.title: Net out-of-plane magnetization at zero field and use of static M
unaddressed_major.why: The 45-degree interpretation is kept and strengthened with a superposition test; nothing touches domains or field history, which a referee raising it would likely have forced into the text.

unaddressed_major.title: Static equilibrium model for sub-picosecond dynamics
unaddressed_major.why: The main text added a sentence on spatial averaging and kept the adiabatic Landau picture; a theorist referee could well have asked and been answered in the letter or SI. Low confidence.

unaddressed_major.title: Heating not quantified
unaddressed_major.why: Heating is a standard referee question for ultrafast claims of non-thermal control; the main text is unchanged, so any answer would sit in the letter or the unseen SI. Low confidence.

unaddressed_major.title: No magnitude estimate; inconsistent THz field values
unaddressed_major.why: 'several V/cm' is unchanged in the main text, which suggests no referee checked it.

unaddressed_major.title: Non-magnetic explanations of saturation
unaddressed_major.why: The saturation argument against surface emission is kept verbatim.

unaddressed_major.title: Model comparison is qualitative but called quantitative
Emission sign and crystal-axis test
unaddressed_major.why: No change to polar plots or orientation reporting.
